content:
#1 Hello, I’m Johannes.

A few days ago I opened a thread here about my Agda project Void and Form. The reactions made clear that I introduced it at the wrong scale. The larger architecture drew attention away from the actual entry point, which is much smaller. This post is only about that entry point.

The motivating pressure comes from a classical idea associated with Leibniz:

If two things cannot be distinguished in any way, on what basis can one still claim that they are really two?

The simplest version of the problem is this.

Two completely identical white sheets of paper lie on a table. What has to be true before one can honestly say:

“There are exactly two sheets here”?

At least two things:

  1. The sheets must not coincide — otherwise there may really be only one.
  2. There must be no hidden third sheet — otherwise the count is not secured.

A stable “two” requires both: non-collapse and no unaccounted surplus.

The companion formalizes exactly that threshold.

Distinction is the condition. Twois what it forces.
Two is the canonical normal form proved from it.
Distinction is the whole condition expressed by that scene: the sheets do not collapse into one, and no hidden third sheet is left unaccounted for. It is the condition under which “exactly two” is a warranted claim rather than a mere naming.

In Agda:

record Distinction : Set₁ where
  field
    S         : Set
    left      : S
    right     : S
    separated : ¬ (left ≡ right)
    cover     : (x : S) → (x ≡ left) ⊎ (x ≡ right)
  • separated is anti-collapse data: the two positions do not coincide.
  • cover is anti-surplus data: nothing else inhabits the carrier.

From this record, the companion proves a uniform two-point normal-form theorem: every Distinction is boundary-preservingly isomorphic to the canonical two-point form Two.

two-normal-form :
  (d : Distinction) → DistinctionIso d Two-distinction

Without separated, the two named positions may collapse into one.
Without cover, the carrier may contain unaccounted points.
Both fields are load-bearing for this threshold.

The development from that record is entirely conditional. What follows from it is machine-checked. What motivates the record itself is the pre-formal question above — and that part Agda does not check.

The checked chain is:

Distinction
  → normal form Two
  → four endomorphisms of Two
  → K4 closure under the stated representation conditions
  → Distinction

The loop closes: the closure presupposes the distinction it was built from.

Relevant places in the companion:

  • Abstract and licensing question
  • Standard-library setting of the compact companion
  • Distinction record

The companion is a compact literate Agda file, type-checked under --safe --without-K. It uses the Agda standard library for basic infrastructure; the larger Void.lagda.tex development rebuilds more of this infrastructure internally.

Companion sources:

  • Literate Agda source (.lagda.tex)
  • Compiled PDF

So my concrete question is:

Is this way of isolating separated and cover as the threshold at which a uniform two-point normal form becomes available already standard in type-theoretic or categorical treatments of binary structure?
subject: What licenses a system to maintain exactly two positions?

content:
#2 Johannes, I tried to indicate it to you before (here), this is the blowing out of proportion of an elementary exercise.

Concerning your question: There are no “treatments of binary structure” anymore than there are books written on the number 2 — not in mathematics anyways, possibly in Sesame Street.

Also mathematical literature does not speak about “thresholds” and so it makes no sense to ask about “known thresholds” here.

You should please take your material to elsewhere, here is not the place for it. And you should definitely not further proliferate the number of nForum threads that you start on this topic.

[edit: The post I am replying to keeps being edited while I write. My reply referred to an earlier version of the question asked. In any case, this discussion is not appropriate here. Johannes should take it to elsewhere.]
subject: What licenses a system to maintain exactly two positions?

content:
#3 I am sorry for the repeated posts. I will leave it here.

[edit: I could not leave the characterization uncorrected. The normalization theorem

(d : Distinction) → DistinctionIso d Two-distinction

concerns the classification of an initially open presentation by a canonical two-point normal form, not an exercise about “the number 2”. The simplicity of the classified object does not determine the mathematical content of the classification.]
subject: What licenses a system to maintain exactly two positions?
